title: Normalized negative Koszul completion model exists and preserves quasi-isomorphisms
statement: Let (C,J,R) be a small ringed site with commutative structure sheaf R [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let A be a commutative ring acting by global sections, and suppose the module category has exact countable products [def-weil-category-product]. Fix a finite ordered list a:Fin r -> A, allowing r=0. For the actual ordered negative Koszul tensor functors K -> K tensor_R tensor_i[R --a_i^(m+1)--> R] [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], there exists a RingedSignedKoszulCompletionModel R rho a with the pure-tensor normalization and all coordinate, transition, product, signed-fibre and unit equations of [def-cbc-signed-koszul-completion-model]. Its fibre functor followed by the ordinary derived-category localization Q [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] inverts every quasi-isomorphism. This is a one-site construction with no coefficient-category functor or comparison as an input or output.

proof.text: Form the actual categorical product of the tensor functors. Define the shift by its projections using the transitions and the diagonal using the empty-subset inclusions. These imply (1-shift) diagonal=0. Form the degreewise binary biproduct B^q plus B^(q-1) with differential (d,0;1-shift,-d), coordinatewise functor action, and unit (diagonal,0). The chain-map equation of the shift cancels the mixed terms in d squared; biproduct and product projection equations verify every model field.

proof.text: The localized countable-product cone is a limit by lem-weil-derived-countable-products-core. Construct the inverse to Q of the product map by the limit universal property using the inverses of its localized level maps. Product projection equations prove both inverse laws, so the product map is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply lem-pe-roos-coordinates-quasi-iso to the explicitly constructed diagonal fibre map and use that Q inverts quasi-isomorphisms.
